title: NOTIFICATION SYSTEM
subtitle: Every service wants to tell users something; the hard parts are slow providers and never sending twice.
footer: DDIA: Ch 5 event-driven messaging · Ch 13 end-to-end idempotency   ·   Similar: Chat app · Job scheduler

items: Accept fast, queue per channel, send with retries
Dedupe, preferences, quiet hours, rate limits before queueing
Priority queues so broadcasts never delay OTPs

blocks.text: Notification service → per-channel queues → workers with backoff → providers; DLQ; delivery log from callbacks.
Direct provider calls: slow checkout, lost messages on outages, no preferences.

items: Idempotency key at intake, delivery log keyed per channel, provider collapse keys.
Circuit breaker, secondary provider for critical messages, expire stale ones.
send_at in UTC per user, released by a scheduler.

blocks.text: "Services get 202 in milliseconds; the notification service dedupes and applies preferences, then per-channel, per-priority queues feed workers with retries and a DLQ, so a marketing broadcast can never delay a password reset."
